Thesis Writing Checklist

A thesis is a long project that lives or dies on structure, and the biggest mistake is treating it as one huge block of writing. This thesis writing checklist breaks it into stages you tackle in order — narrowing a question, planning research, drafting chapter by chapter, then editing and formatting for submission. Work through it in sequence, and see more study and exam checklists.

verified Curated by the Gisti team · Updated July 2026

Thesis Writing Checklist · 16 items

  1. 1
    Choose and narrow your topic into a specific, answerable research question

    Too broad is the number-one reason a thesis stalls.

  2. 2
    Confirm your supervisor and agree on scope, expectations, and a rough timeline
  3. 3
    Do a literature review and map what has already been written on your question

    Note the gap your work will fill.

  4. 4
    Write and get approval for your proposal or research plan
  5. 5
    Choose your methodology and, if needed, get ethics or data approval

    Ethics review can take weeks — start it early.

  6. 6
    Set up a reference manager and log every source as you read

    A citation manager saves days of cleanup later — set it up before you read.

  7. 7
    Build a chapter outline with a target word count for each section
  8. 8
    Collect and analyze your data or primary material
  9. 9
    Draft the body chapters first — methods, results, and discussion

    The introduction is easiest to write once you know what you found.

  10. 10
    Write the introduction and literature review to frame the finished body
  11. 11
    Write the conclusion, tying findings back to your original question
  12. 12
    Write the abstract last, summarizing the whole thesis in one page
  13. 13
    Revise for argument and structure — does each chapter earn its place?

    Fix the big-picture flow before line-editing.

  14. 14
    Proofread for grammar, and check every citation and reference for accuracy
  15. 15
    Format to your department's guidelines: title page, contents, margins, and numbering

    Follow the official template exactly — formatting rejections cost time.

  16. 16
    Run a final plagiarism check and submit before the deadline, keeping a backup copy

    Submit a day early to absorb any upload problems.

Frequently asked questions

How do I start writing a thesis? expand_more

Start by narrowing a broad interest into one specific, answerable research question, then agree the scope with your supervisor. Do a literature review to see what already exists and where your work fits, and write a proposal before any real writing. A clear question and an approved plan prevent the most common cause of a stalled thesis.

In what order should I write thesis chapters? expand_more

Write the body chapters first — methodology, results, and discussion — because they are grounded in your actual work. Then write the introduction and literature review to frame what the reader is about to see, followed by the conclusion. Write the abstract last, once the whole thesis exists to summarize.

How long does it take to write a thesis? expand_more

It varies widely by level and field, but a master's thesis often takes three to six months of focused work and a doctoral thesis a year or more. The writing itself is only part of it — research, data collection, ethics approval, and multiple rounds of editing all take time, which is why a timeline and an early start matter so much.
